KEF LS LUXE Review – The Real Future of High-End HiFi?

KEF LS LUXE Review – The Future of High-End Wireless HiFi?

Stereo Systems & Components

There was a time when “wireless speaker” meant compromise. Convenience came at the expense of musicality, soundstage, refinement, and ultimately the emotional connection that keeps us glued to our favorite albums for hours.

Those days are rapidly disappearing.

The Video Review 
KEF has spent years proving that active, streaming loudspeakers can be serious audiophile products, beginning with the LS50 Wireless and continuing through the impressive LS60 Wireless. Now comes the LS LUXE, a speaker that isn’t simply another update—it represents what may be the company’s most ambitious all-in-one music system to date. I have had these here for a few weeks now and have had to keep it quiet until the release date. Now I am ready to talk about these lovely jewel like speakers that not only put out such an incredible sound, they are easy as pie to set up.

The LS Luxe in the new Listening Room. Well this is a rendering of what it will soon look like. 

Audio Equipment

I once owned the now famous and what some consider “legendary” LS 50 speakers and had them in the passive and wireless versions. The passive were great, if and only if you found a room and amp that played well with them. If you did, they were little beasts that performed to a very high level for their size. The issue for me with the LS50 was the bass output was on the lighter side where the treble was well, highlighted in a way that was almost “too much”. Again though, it was probably a mismatch to my then amplifier.

Video Review of the LS Luxe

Speakers

I have heard the LS50 sound pretty amazing with some blues one day at a shop but I was never able to get them to sound that good in my room, which at the time was a tiny 12X13.

The wireless LS 50 were speakers I enjoyed more than the passive as the amps and everything built into them was designed to power that speaker just right. Synergy built in so to speak. Even so, looking back at those little LS 50 wireless speakers they were also a little on the dry side for me. I like it big, bold, meaty and moist vs dry and etched.

The good news is that the LS Luxe is different from the LS 50 in almost every way and they sound nothing alike to me. Yes, the LS Luxe (f0r me) is a much bigger, deeper and more spatial and transparent sounding speaker. An entirely new animal and one that the audio world should take seriously as we may truly be looking at the future of this hobby. Wireless without compromise? These LS Luxe get as close to this goal as I have ever heard.

Bookshelf Speakers

The previous LS 50 in green 

The LS Luxe are speakers that need nothing to play gorgeous high end music besides two power outlets and an internet connection. No amp, preamp, DAC or streamer is needed here and the savings can be pretty substantial. It’s all here, built in, and while the LS Luxe are in a more pricey cost bracket vs the older LS 50, they are well worth the extra cost. I consider the $3999 price tag to be quite the deal on the LS Luxe as they perform more like a set that costs double.

Physics

I am truly excited about the LS Luxe as the design, build quality. function, ease of use and most importantly, the sound quality is all top tier here. These easily compete with higher cost systems that use many boxes to create the musical picture yet the Luxe are completely wireless and do not even need to be connected to each other. Just unbox from the luxurious packaging and plug each speaker into a power outlet. Download the KEF app and setup takes just a few minutes. Then you can instantly stream audiophile quality music via any of the major streaming services.

Tidal Connect. Qobuz Connect. Spotify Connect. Airplay and more.

The KEF LS Luxe are also quite luxurious and feel and look like a true high end product. IN other words you will be surprised when you unbox them and see just what you are getting for the money. No disappointments but I would never expect to be let down with a new KEF product anyway.

At around $4,000 per pair, the LS LUXE sits in an interesting position. It’s priced well above lifestyle wireless speakers but well below many traditional audiophile systems once amplification, DACs, streamers, cables, and stands are factored into the equation.

The obvious question is simple:

Can a single purchase really replace an entire high-end stereo system?

After spending time living with the LS LUXE, I believe KEF has come closer than ever to making that answer a confident “yes.” The sound quality is open, large, spatial and deep. KEF is also proving with the LS Luxe that big serious bass performance is no longer just reserved for large speakers. The bass here is absolutely insane and these fill my mid sized room with ease. There is some warmth here with a superb transparency as well but these are not sharp or bass shy in any way.

Amplifiers

LS Luxe comes in three colors. 

Beautiful Industrial Design

The first thing you’ll notice is that these don’t really resemble traditional bookshelf speakers. They are rounded. shapely and svelte.

Speakers

Rather than another square cabinet, KEF partnered with renowned industrial designer Ross Lovegrove to create something far more sculptural. The LS Luxe appear organic and in a moulded form meant to stand in the middle of a room and be admired for their shapely design. They come in three colors which are Dusk Titanium, Eclipse Black and Mineral White. I have the Mineral White here with me now.

The big news here though is VECO — a new bass technology KEF say is a first for a wireless HiFi speaker.
Basically a sensor watches how the bass cone is moving and actually corrects it in real time, so the bass stays tight and controlled when you turn it up, instead of going soft the way small speakers usually do.
Every curve appears to be done with intent and the cabinet itself almost looks like it was carved from a single piece rather than assembled from panels. The finish quality is exceptional, and these are speakers you’ll proudly display rather than hide away in a listening room.

The organic shape isn’t simply about aesthetics either. The cabinet construction is designed to minimize unwanted resonances while creating an enclosure that’s both extremely rigid and visually striking. It’s one of the more premium-looking wireless systems currently available.

Technology Beneath the Surface

Bookshelf Speakers

KEF didn’t simply redesign the cabinet.

Inside the LS LUXE is an entirely new generation of engineering that combines the company’s latest Uni-Q driver array with Metamaterial Absorption Technology (MAT), helping reduce unwanted high-frequency reflections behind the tweeter for greater clarity and openness. As already mentioned the speakers also introduce KEF’s Velocity Control Technology (VECO), which continuously monitors bass driver motion in real time to reduce distortion and improve low-frequency accuracy.

Power is equally impressive.

Each speaker houses dedicated amplification with 280 watts of Class D power for the bass driver and 100 watts of Class A/B amplification for the high frequencies, allowing each driver to operate under optimal conditions without the compromises found in passive crossover designs. This is sort of a secret sauce IMO.

The result is a fully active loudspeaker that has complete control over every driver, every crossover point, and every watt of available power.

While KEF sells dedicated stands for the LS Luxe I did not receive them so am using some old Dynaudio stands here. 

Streaming Done Right

Perhaps one of the biggest strengths of the LS LUXE is that virtually everything today’s music lover needs is already built in.

Audio Equipment

Whether your library lives on Tidal, Qobuz, Spotify Connect, AirPlay 2, Chromecast, Bluetooth, or local network storage, the LS LUXE supports nearly every modern playback option. HDMI eARC allows the speakers to become an elegant television audio solution while USB-C, optical, coaxial, and analogue inputs provide flexibility for traditional components as well. Hi-resolution playback extends up to 24-bit/384kHz with DSD128 support.

I tested these in my new audio room and they made magic in this space with a full bodied, deeply rich and fluid musical presentation. Imaging was superb bringing vocals out into the space a bit from the speakers while the stage grew tall and wide.

Moving them over to my TV using HDMI I was treated to mind blowing sound from movies and damn, it was explosive and powerful when turned up. The beauty of the LS Luxe is more than just two channel music, these can do it all and do it with ease. The dual amps in each speaker are pretty insane as well with almost 300 watts of class D to the mid and bass driver and 100 watts of Class A/B to the tweeter. This hybrid approach works well as it keeps the treble from getting that class D dullness. Brilliant! This is why I called it the “secret sauce” as I find many class D amps can soften the treble, some even dull it. The way KEF did this ensures the treble stays airy and extended yet the bass and mids benefit from that class D power.

The LS Luxe are so versatile and for many listeners, this means eliminating an equipment rack filled with separate components.

Electronic Components

No external DAC.

No integrated amplifier.

No streamer.

Just connect, configure, and enjoy.

Listening Impressions

The hallmark of nearly every great KEF loudspeaker has always been imaging, and the LS LUXE proudly continues that tradition.

Physics

The Uni-Q driver creates a wonderfully coherent presentation where voices and instruments emerge from an exceptionally stable center image. Instead of hearing separate drivers handing music back and forth, everything arrives with remarkable consistency.

Vocals sound focused, three dimensional and natural. Also they are nicely imaged, meaning the vocals will be in the center of the soundstage image.

Acoustic instruments possess convincing body and texture and this is important as real instruments have body and texture.

Percussion carries excellent transient speed without becoming sharp or fatiguing. In fact drums are big and bold, with a big bodied soulful punch.

Perhaps even more impressive is how effortless these speakers sound. Dynamics arrive without strain, allowing quiet passages to remain delicate while larger orchestral crescendos and energetic rock recordings expand with confidence.

Bass performance is another pleasant surprise. Considering the relatively compact cabinets, extension is satisfying, while control remains excellent. KEF’s new driver control technology seems to pay dividends here, producing low frequencies that sound tight, articulate, and composed rather than exaggerated. Deep..immersive and rich is what I hear with the bass. No deficiencies at all.

Stereo Systems & Components

The presentation leans toward neutrality with slight warmth (really will depend on the room you place them in), yet it never feels clinical. There’s an inviting musicality that encourages long listening sessions without fatigue.

Soundstage width extends well beyond the cabinets, while depth layering gives recordings an impressive sense of dimensionality. Close your eyes, and these disappear far better than one might expect from an active wireless system.

If I can be honest I have to say that KEF knocked it out of the park here with the Luxe. They are more than just a pretty face and over the weeks I listened to them in my old and new audio room they always impressed, and I mean in a big way. The sound was just so high end yet coming from a set of $4k all in one speakers. Whether I watched a movie using them or listened to high res recordings from Tidal or Qobuz the music immersed me into it. Never heard a wireless speaker of this size sound anything like this one.

Setup and Everyday Use

Speakers

One of the greatest compliments I can give the LS LUXE is that they simply stay out of your way.

Setup is straightforward using KEF’s Connect app, and once configured the system feels mature, responsive, and intuitive. Room EQ options allow users to tailor bass response for their listening space, helping extract the best performance regardless of placement.

This is exactly how modern HiFi should behave.

You spend your time listening to music—not troubleshooting components. You do not need noise, heat or trouble and the LS Luxe brings none of these things. 

The LUXE also ships with a nice remote that has all of the controls you need such as power, volume, mute, input selection and it also allows you to skip tracks without having to use your phone. I love cueing up one of my playlists, sitting back and having the ease of skipping a track without having to have my phone open.

There is also a sub output on the speaker so if you choose to add a sub (I do not need one here) it is easy to do.

Who Are These For?

The LS LUXE occupies a fascinating niche.

Amplifiers

Traditional audiophiles may appreciate the engineering, imaging precision, and refinement while newer music lovers may simply appreciate having world-class sound without building an elaborate component system.

These are equally comfortable in a dedicated listening room, an upscale living room, a modern apartment, or even a luxury office.

For someone starting from scratch, they represent one of the cleanest and most beautiful paths into genuine high-end audio. Believe me when I say that I have heard hundreds of systems in my life. What I see today in this hobby is encouraging and KEF is one of those companies leading the way for modern HiFi. Many today want simple, small and do not want to compromise when it comes to sound or function. The LS Luxe are perfect for anyone who seeks this. No they are not as all out resolute or polished as my reference setup that has a $45k price tag but that doesn’t matter. The LS Luxe brings the music to me in a similar way, just with a different flavor. That is impressive.

These are the best sounding and easiest to set up wireless speakers I have ever heard. Period. 

Final Thoughts

KEF has never been afraid to challenge the traditional HiFi formula, and the LS LUXE may be their most convincing argument yet that fewer boxes don’t necessarily mean lower performance. By combining outstanding industrial design, sophisticated acoustic engineering, robust streaming capabilities, and genuinely audiophile sound quality into one elegant package, the LS LUXE delivers an experience that feels remarkably complete.

Electronic Components

Will it replace a carefully assembled six-figure reference system?

Of course not.

But that’s also missing the point.

The LS LUXE offers something arguably more valuable for many listeners: extraordinary performance with almost none of the complexity that has traditionally accompanied high-end audio. It’s elegant, beautifully engineered, wonderfully musical, and refreshingly easy to live with. The fact that they used a class A/B amp for the tweeter and a class D for the mid/bass says they really know what they are doing. This allows the treble to be airy while the midrange is slightly warm and earthy with a stunning reproduction of 3D space.

For anyone looking to simplify their system without sacrificing serious sound quality, the KEF LS LUXE deserves a place near the very top of the audition list. I feel these will be a smash hit for KEF and rightly so.
